title: A qcqs overlap detects matching after every base change
statement: Let S be any scheme and W,U,V qcqs etale objects over S, with maps f : U → W and g : V → W. There exist a qcqs etale object Z and arrows p : Z → U, q : Z → V satisfying pf=qg such that the following holds. For any scheme T, h : T → S, sheaf of sets F on T, and sections s,t on U_T,V_T, equality of their restrictions to Z_T implies equality of their restrictions along any a : Y → U_T, a′ : Y → V_T with af_T=a′g_T, for any etale Y over T.

source.document: Stacks Project, Étale Cohomology, Tags 03Q4 and 09YQ

proof.text: Take Z to be the scheme pullback of f.left and g.left, with structure map its first projection followed by U.hom. Its two projections define maps p,q of etale objects, and pullback.condition gives pf=qg. The arrow g.left is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by cancellation against W.hom; stability under base change and composition make Z.hom qcqs.

Given a,a′ after an arbitrary base change h, compose their underlying arrows with the first projections back to U,V. Their composites to W agree by the hypothesis. Lift this pair into Z, then lift that arrow together with Y.hom into Z ×_S T. The two pullback projection identities prove that the resulting v has composites a,a′ with the base changes of p,q. Restrict the equality on Z_T along v and use presheaf functoriality.
